answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because sable only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, ripple is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any quill approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
